Check: Is there a documented owner (CoE or platform team) with a defined RACI between IT, security, compliance and the business? Is there an executive sponsor?
Verify: Interview platform owner; review charter, org chart, RACI
Target: Target: named sponsor, CoE lead, security liaison. Red flag: governance is informal or sits with whoever is admin

Check: Are use cases tiered (personal productivity, team, enterprise/pro-dev) with different environments, connectors, review and ALM rules for each tier?
Verify: Compare zone definitions to the actual environment and policy inventory (see Learn: Implement a zoned governance strategy)
Target: Each zone maps to an environment type, data policy, sharing limit and review path. Red flag: one policy for everything

Check: Do makers complete training and acknowledge policies before getting build access? Is a maker welcome message configured?
Verify: PPAC maker welcome content; training and LMS records
Target: Makers know where to build, what data is allowed and who to call. Red flag: access by default, no training

Check: Is there a request path for production environments, premium or custom connectors, HTTP calls, external-facing agents and autonomous agents? Are SLAs defined?
Verify: Ticketing system, approval records, sample of last 10 requests
Target: Reviewed within a defined SLA with security sign-off for high-risk patterns. Red flag: shadow production workloads

Check: Are DLP, sharing and connector exceptions recorded with an owner, rationale and expiry date?
Verify: Exception register; compare to policy configuration in PPAC
Target: All exceptions time-bound and reviewed at least quarterly. Red flag: permanent undocumented exemptions

Check: Is there a complete, current inventory of apps, flows, agents, connections, connectors, environments and makers, including orphans?
Verify: PPAC inventory, admin PowerShell (Get-AdminPowerApp, Get-AdminFlow), Dataverse bot table
Target: Inventory refreshed at least weekly and reconciled to owners. Red flag: inventory is a spreadsheet or does not exist

Check: Are agents from Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot (declarative and agent-builder agents) and Foundry tracked in one registry with an owner each? Has Microsoft Agent 365 been evaluated as a control plane?
Verify: Microsoft 365 admin center Agents area; Agent 365 documentation (verify current availability and licensing)
Target: One agent registry with ownership and lifecycle state. Red flag: agents visible only to their makers

Check: Is the corporate data classification mapped to connector groups (Business, Non-business, Blocked) and to sensitivity labels?
Verify: Classification policy vs data policy configuration
Target: Mapping is documented and tested. Red flag: connector groups chosen by convenience

Check: Who holds Global Admin, Power Platform Admin and Dynamics 365 Admin? Could Environment Admin or System Administrator be used instead? Do any environments have more than 10 admins?
Verify: Entra admin roles; PPAC Security > Overview (the administrator privileges recommendation fires above 10)
Target: Few, named, least-privilege roles. Red flag: dozens of permanent admins

Check: Are high-privilege roles eligible (just-in-time) with MFA and approval instead of standing? Is there a tested break-glass process?
Verify: Entra PIM role settings and audit history
Target: No standing Power Platform Administrator access. Red flag: permanent assignment, shared admin accounts

Check: Review PPAC Settings: who can create environments, trial and developer environments, share apps with Everyone, use guests, and use AI features; cross-geo data movement for generative AI.
Verify: PPAC > Settings; Get-TenantSettings output exported and diffed against a baseline
Target: Settings match the documented baseline. Red flag: defaults never reviewed

Check: Is creation of production, sandbox, trial and developer environments limited to admins?
Verify: PPAC Settings > Tenant settings (environment creation); check count of trial/personal environments created last 90 days
Target: Admins only, with a request process. Red flag: any licensed user can create

Check: Are cross-tenant inbound and outbound connections restricted to an explicit allow-list of tenants?
Verify: PPAC > Security > Identity and access; Get-PowerAppTenantIsolationPolicy. Note: the Copilot Studio security FAQ states Copilot Studio does not support tenant isolation, so compensate with data policies and endpoint filtering
Target: Isolation on with a named allow-list. Red flag: off (default allows cross-tenant connections)

Check: Is tenant-level analytics on? Are the Security > Overview recommendations reviewed and dismissals justified?
Verify: PPAC > Security > Overview. The security score is a preview feature intended for evaluation, so use it as a prompt, not a metric of record
Target: Recommendations triaged monthly. Red flag: analytics off, no review

Check: Can users self-start trials or sign up for Copilot Studio or Power Platform licenses outside IT?
Verify: Entra self-service sign-up settings; Copilot Studio self-service trial controls; MSCommerce policy
Target: Blocked or governed. Red flag: shadow tenants of makers and unmanaged trial environments

Check: Is Customer Lockbox decided and documented? Are admins subscribed to message center and service health?
Verify: PPAC Security > Compliance; Microsoft 365 message center. Lockbox does not cover audit-logging telemetry or Agent 365 governance events
Target: Decision recorded with scope limits understood. Red flag: assumed to cover everything

Check: Is the default environment renamed, managed, covered by a restrictive data policy, sharing limits and welcome content? Are production workloads present?
Verify: PPAC Environments; inventory of apps, flows and agents by environment (Learn: Secure the default environment)
Target: Personal productivity only; ACP blocks all connectors where managed. Red flag: business-critical assets in default

Check: For each environment: type (production, sandbox, developer, trial, default), owner, region, security group, solution count, last activity.
Verify: PPAC Environments; Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment; Power Platform inventory
Target: No environment without owner and purpose. Red flag: unknown or ownerless environments

Check: Are workloads developed in dev, validated in test and run in production? Are makers prevented from editing production directly?
Verify: Review solution layering, production environment maker roles, pipeline history
Target: Makers hold no maker role in production. Red flag: edits made directly in prod

Check: What percentage of environments, and which production environments, are managed? Which managed-only controls are actually configured (sharing limits, solution checker, IP firewall, cookie binding, CMK, Lockbox, extended backup)?
Verify: PPAC > Security > Overview (percentage unmanaged); environment details
Target: All production environments managed with features configured. Red flag: managed in name only

Check: Microsoft documents that unmanaged developer environments are deprecated and must have Managed Environments enabled before 15 December 2026 to be kept. Which developer environments are still unmanaged?
Verify: PPAC Environments filtered by type = Developer and managed = No; confirm the latest date on Learn (Managed environments overview)
Target: Decision made and executed for each one. Red flag: no plan, losing maker work

Check: Is default environment routing on so new makers land in their own developer environment instead of the shared default environment? Is a maker welcome message configured?
Verify: PPAC Settings > Environment routing and Maker welcome content
Target: On for Copilot Studio and Power Apps makers. Red flag: everyone builds in default

Check: Are environments organized into groups with rules (sharing, solution checker, maker welcome, maker credential options, AI features)?
Verify: PPAC Environment groups and Rules
Target: Groups reflect zones. Red flag: every environment configured by hand

Check: Is access to each Dataverse environment restricted to an Entra security group? Is the admin count controlled?
Verify: Environment settings; PPAC security recommendation for environments without a security group
Target: Security group on all production environments. Red flag: any licensed user can enter

Check: Are trial, inactive and abandoned environments detected and removed? Is storage consumption tracked?
Verify: Power Platform inventory, PPAC capacity, environment last-activity dates
Target: Quarterly clean-up. Red flag: hundreds of stale trial environments

Check: Is there a tenant-scoped data policy covering all environments, including new ones? Which group is the default for new connectors?
Verify: PPAC Data policies; Get-DlpPolicy
Target: Baseline exists; default group Blocked or deliberate. Red flag: no tenant policy, or environments excluded without reason

Check: Is each connector classified Business, Non-business or Blocked with a documented reason? Are high-risk connectors (HTTP, SMTP, FTP, personal storage, social) handled explicitly?
Verify: Export all policies; review classification list against the data classification standard
Target: Classification traceable to policy. Red flag: Business group contains consumer or external services

Check: How are newly released connectors handled? Connectors released after 2019 (including several Copilot Studio ones) default to Non-business unless the default group is changed.
Verify: PPAC Data policies > default group setting; compare connector list to last review
Target: Default Blocked for restrictive policies. Red flag: new connectors usable on day one

Check: Are there stricter policies for the default environment and relaxed, reviewed policies for approved production environments?
Verify: Policy scope per environment; zoned governance mapping
Target: Policy per zone. Red flag: one global policy forced to be permissive

Check: Where managed, is the default environment configured to block all connectors (empty Business and Non-business groups, all blocked)?
Verify: PPAC Advanced connector policies; known limitations in Learn
Target: ACP used where possible. Red flag: manual allow-list drift

Check: Can makers create custom connectors? Are HTTP, custom connector and public-website endpoints restricted by URL pattern, with HTTPS only?
Verify: PPAC connector endpoint filtering and custom connector rules
Target: Allow or deny by pattern. Red flag: any endpoint reachable from HTTP node or custom connector

Check: Is the connector Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio blocked so agents cannot publish without sign-in?
Verify: Data policy connector list; test with a sandbox agent set to No authentication (publish should be blocked)
Target: Blocked in every environment where agents are built, except approved public-facing exceptions. Red flag: anonymous agents possible

Feature: Copilot Studio channel, skill and trigger controls
Check: Are only approved channels allowed (Teams and Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Direct Line, Omnichannel, Facebook, WhatsApp)? Are Skills with Copilot Studio, HTTP, Application Insights and event triggers (Microsoft Copilot Studio connector) controlled? Note Direct Line is allowed by default.
Verify: Data policy connector list; Channels page error details in Copilot Studio
Target: Unused channels and capabilities blocked. Red flag: every channel open

Check: Are SharePoint and public-website knowledge sources governed with endpoint filtering? Is the public-data (Bing) option controlled per environment?
Verify: Data policy endpoint rules; environment generative AI settings
Target: Approved sites only for public knowledge. Red flag: unrestricted web grounding

Check: Are policy changes audited, tested in a sandbox and reviewed at least quarterly? Is the data-policy error message customized with contact details?
Verify: Purview audit for policy changes; Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings
Target: Change control with owner. Red flag: undocumented edits, silent breakage of apps

Check: Do Exchange transport rules limit automated external send and forward from flows and apps (using x-ms-mail-application headers)?
Verify: Exchange admin center mail flow rules (Learn: Secure the default environment)
Target: External send blocked except from an allow-list. Red flag: any flow can mail externally

Check: Are data policies applied to desktop flows and RPA connectors?
Verify: PPAC desktop flow data policy settings
Target: Same rigor as cloud flows. Red flag: RPA outside policy

Check: Do Conditional Access policies (MFA, device compliance, location, sign-in risk) cover Power Platform, Dataverse and Copilot Studio for makers, admins and end users?
Verify: Entra Conditional Access, What If tool, sign-in logs
Target: No unmanaged-device admin access. Red flag: exclusions for convenience, legacy auth allowed

Check: For every agent: Authenticate with Microsoft (default), manual Entra ID, or No authentication? Is SSO configured? Is certificate-based manual authentication used where required?
Verify: Copilot Studio > Settings > Security > Authentication; Dataverse bot table query; security scan warnings
Target: Authenticated by default. Red flag: No authentication on anything that can reach internal data

Check: Is Control maker credential options set (end-user only, maker only, or both) at environment or group level? Which agents and flows currently use maker credentials? Note: by default both are enabled, and enforcing end-user credentials breaks scheduled or autonomous agents.
Verify: PPAC > Environment or group > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents
Target: End-user credentials by default; maker credentials only by exception with reviewed scope. Red flag: agent runs as maker with broad access

Check: Inventory application users and app registrations used by flows, connectors and CI/CD. Check owners, secret and certificate expiry, permissions and Conditional Access for workload identities.
Verify: Entra app registrations; PPAC Application users; Microsoft Graph
Target: Certificates or federated credentials; least privilege; two owners. Red flag: long-lived secrets in flows

Check: Do production connections use personal accounts, shared mailboxes or service accounts? Are service accounts licensed, MFA-compliant, rotated and owned?
Verify: Connections list per environment; Get-AdminPowerAppConnection; interview
Target: Dedicated, governed service identities. Red flag: flow dies when an employee leaves

Check: Which connections are shared or embedded in apps and agents? Which belong to disabled or departed users?
Verify: Admin connection inventory; PPAC
Target: No connection owned by disabled account. Red flag: broad data access via borrowed connection

Check: Can guests build or use Power Platform assets? Is restricted guest access on for environments? Does Everyone sharing include guests (it does)?
Verify: PPAC environment settings; Entra external collaboration settings
Target: Guests restricted and reviewed. Red flag: Everyone sharing enabled

Check: Are environment roles and security groups reviewed regularly? Is ownership of apps, flows and agents transferred on leave?
Verify: Entra access reviews; offboarding procedure; orphan report
Target: Quarterly review and automated reassignment. Red flag: hundreds of ownerless assets

Check: If Microsoft Agent 365 or Entra agent identities are in use, are they governed with Conditional Access, access governance and lifecycle? (Verify current availability, preview status and licensing.)
Verify: Agent 365 and Entra documentation; admin centers
Target: Agents treated as identities. Red flag: agents with undefined permissions

Check: Do connectors, HTTP calls and custom connectors use OAuth, managed identity or Key Vault rather than keys stored in the asset?
Verify: Review environment variables (secret type), custom connector auth, flow definitions
Target: No secrets in code or topics. Red flag: API keys in variables or compose actions

Check: Are custom roles built on least privilege? How many users hold System Administrator or System Customizer? Are roles reviewed?
Verify: Environment > Users + Security roles export; compare role privileges to job functions
Target: Minimal admin roles. Red flag: System Administrator as default makers' role in production

Check: Do business units, teams and record ownership reflect the data boundary? Are access teams or security groups used?
Verify: Dataverse business unit and team structure
Target: Structure mirrors data ownership. Red flag: single root business unit with organization-wide read

Check: Are sensitive columns (PII, financial, health) protected with column security profiles?
Verify: Dataverse column security; data classification
Target: Sensitive columns restricted. Red flag: PII visible to all roles

Check: Is Dataverse auditing on at environment, table and column level? How long are logs retained and who reviews them?
Verify: Environment settings > Audit; Purview audit
Target: Auditing on for sensitive tables; retention matches policy. Red flag: off

Check: Who can read the Conversation Transcript table? How long are transcripts retained? Do transcripts contain PII or secrets that users typed?
Verify: Dataverse security roles for Conversation Transcript; Copilot Studio analytics settings; retention settings
Target: Limited access, defined retention. Red flag: broad read access, indefinite retention

Check: Is IP firewall enabled for Dataverse and IP address-based cookie binding configured? (Managed Environments feature.)
Verify: PPAC environment settings; security recommendations
Target: On for sensitive environments. Red flag: not configured

Check: Is virtual network support configured where agents or flows must reach private data sources?
Verify: PPAC Virtual network policies; Azure networking
Target: Private connectivity for private data. Red flag: private data exposed through public endpoints

Check: Are CMK and Customer Lockbox required for regulated data? If CMK is used, does it include Copilot Studio data? Are key rotation and recovery tested?
Verify: PPAC Security > Data and privacy; Key Vault; Learn CMK pages
Target: Documented decision and tested recovery. Red flag: CMK on with no key recovery process

Check: What are backup retention settings? Are manual backups taken before major change? Is extended retention used for regulated environments?
Verify: PPAC Backups; DR runbook
Target: Tested restore. Red flag: restore never tested

Check: Are Purview sensitivity labels and data masking rules used where available?
Verify: Purview; Managed Environment masking rules (verify availability)
Target: Labels respected by agents. Red flag: unlabeled sensitive content

Check: Is Share with Everyone disabled? Are sharing limits set in managed environments (individual and group limits)? Are security groups used instead of individuals?
Verify: Get-TenantSettings (disableShareWithEveryone); PPAC > Environment > Edit managed environment > Limit sharing
Target: Everyone disabled; limits set. Red flag: large unmanaged sharing, guests included

Check: Do canvas apps use the author's connection (implicit sharing) to access data users would not otherwise reach?
Verify: App connection details; admin connection inventory; sample critical apps
Target: Users authenticate or use governed service connection. Red flag: app gives everyone the author's data access

Check: Are production apps in solutions and owned by teams or service identities rather than a single user?
Verify: Power Platform inventory; solution inventory; owner report
Target: No business-critical app outside a solution. Red flag: apps in My apps owned by an individual

Check: Which apps are owned by disabled accounts or unused for 90+ days?
Verify: Power Platform inventory; Advisor and PPAC app usage analytics
Target: Archive or reassign monthly. Red flag: many dormant apps with live connections

Check: Are Power Apps component framework (PCF) components and code apps allow-listed and reviewed? Who can import them?
Verify: PPAC environment feature settings; managed environment control of allowed apps; code review
Target: Allow-list and review. Red flag: arbitrary components in production

Check: Is solution checker enforcement configured in managed environments? Are critical rules enforced?
Verify: PPAC Managed Environment > Solution checker
Target: Block deploy on high-severity findings. Red flag: not enabled

Check: For sensitive apps, are granular Conditional Access policies applied (verify current status of app-level controls)?
Verify: PPAC admin apps; Entra authentication contexts
Target: Sensitive apps require stronger auth. Red flag: same access as every other app

Check: Are secrets, API keys or sensitive data hard-coded in app formulas, variables or collections? Is data filtered server side or only hidden client side?
Verify: Review critical apps; app checker; code scanning where available
Target: No secrets; server-side filtering. Red flag: hidden controls as security

Check: For each site: anonymous access, web roles, table permissions, form and list exposure, WAF and CDN, secure configuration review.
Verify: Power Pages admin center; security scan; maker review of table permissions
Target: Least-privilege permissions, security scan clean. Red flag: anonymous read of Dataverse tables

Check: Is Application Insights or monitoring configured for critical apps?
Verify: App settings; Azure Monitor
Target: Errors and performance observable. Red flag: no telemetry on critical apps

Check: Are production flows in solutions, owned by teams or service identities, with co-owners? Which flows are owned by disabled users?
Verify: Get-AdminFlow, Get-AdminFlowOwnerRole; Power Platform inventory
Target: All production flows in solutions. Red flag: critical flows in My flows

Check: Who can call each When an HTTP request is received trigger (any user in tenant, specific users, or anyone)? Is the trigger URL protected and rotated?
Verify: Flow definition review; filter inventory for HTTP triggers
Target: Authenticated callers only. Red flag: anonymous URL exposed to the internet

Check: Are credentials, tokens or keys stored in compose actions, variables or connections? Is Key Vault or secret-type environment variable used?
Verify: Flow definition export search; Environment variables
Target: No secrets in definitions. Red flag: plaintext keys

Check: How are run-only users configured (use my connection vs. their own)? Which flows give users indirect access to data they could not otherwise reach?
Verify: Flow sharing settings; sample of high-privilege flows
Target: User connections where appropriate. Red flag: run-only users gain author's permissions

Check: Do actions that handle PII or secrets have secure inputs and outputs on? Who can see run history?
Verify: Flow action settings; run history access
Target: Sensitive actions masked. Red flag: PII visible in run history

Check: Which flows send external email, Teams messages, push to SaaS, or call external HTTP endpoints? Are these allowed by data policy and Exchange rules?
Verify: Inventory flows using Office 365 Outlook, HTTP, SMTP, SFTP; Exchange mail flow rules
Target: Reviewed and allow-listed. Red flag: mass mail from personal flow

Check: Are approvers validated? Do flows auto-approve high-impact actions? Is delegation controlled?
Verify: Approval flow review
Target: Human approval for material actions. Red flag: automated approval of sensitive changes

Check: Do flows have scopes, run-after logic, retries, alerts and ownership notifications? Are suspended flows detected?
Verify: Flow analytics; failure notifications
Target: Failures reach an owner. Red flag: silent failure of finance or HR processes

Check: Are machines and machine groups governed, credentials stored securely, unattended runs approved, and data policies applied? Who can run flows on which machines?
Verify: Power Automate machine management; Windows machine hardening; PPAC desktop flow data policy
Target: Hardened machines, vaulted credentials, least privilege. Red flag: shared admin accounts on RPA machines

Check: Are flows aligned to the right licensing (per user, per flow, process)? Are API request limits and concurrency considered?
Verify: PPAC capacity; license reports; request limits page
Target: No unlicensed premium use. Red flag: throttling in business-critical flows

Check: List every agent and its authentication mode. Are any set to No authentication? Is the default Authenticate with Microsoft used, and is Entra ID v2 manual authentication configured correctly (scopes, token exchange, SSO)?
Verify: Copilot Studio > Security > Authentication; Dataverse bot table; Learn: Configure user authentication
Target: All internal agents authenticated. Red flag: anonymous agents with internal knowledge or tools

Check: Where is each agent published: Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, SharePoint, Demo website, custom website (Direct Line), WhatsApp, Facebook, Omnichannel? Are unused channels blocked by data policy?
Verify: Copilot Studio Channels; data policy channel connectors
Target: Only needed channels allowed. Red flag: demo website or open web channel on internal agents

Check: For website embedding, are Direct Line secrets avoided in client code? Is secured web channel access (token endpoint, authenticated sessions) enforced?
Verify: Copilot Studio > Settings > Security > Web channel security (Learn: Configure web channel security)
Target: Token-based, short-lived access. Red flag: Direct Line secret in page source

Check: How broadly is each agent shared? Is it shared with everyone in the organization? How many co-authors? Are security groups used? Who can read transcripts?
Verify: Copilot Studio > Share; Dataverse security roles; security scan warning for sharing with everyone
Target: Security-group sharing with owner and backup owner. Red flag: share with everyone by default

Check: Do agents publish with active security scan warnings (no authentication, maker-provided credentials, shared with everyone)? Are warnings tracked?
Verify: Copilot Studio security scan and agent runtime protection status; Learn: Automatic security scan
Target: Zero unexplained warnings. Red flag: makers ignore warnings

Feature: Generative AI and web grounding settings
Check: Are generative AI features, public-web (Bing) grounding and cross-geo data movement set deliberately per environment? Is tenant-level publishing of generative-AI agents allowed intentionally?
Verify: PPAC Copilot settings (tenant and environment); Learn: Security FAQ
Target: Settings match zone. Red flag: defaults for every environment

Check: Do topics store PII or secrets in variables? Do HTTP request nodes call unreviewed external endpoints? Are credentials hard-coded?
Verify: Agent export / solution review; HTTP node inventory
Target: No secrets; endpoints allow-listed. Red flag: API key in topic

Check: Who has the roles that allow creating, reading, updating and deleting agents (Copilot, Copilot Subcomponent, Conversation Transcript tables)? Is System Administrator used instead?
Verify: Environment security roles; zoned governance table of maker access controls
Target: Scoped maker roles. Red flag: System Administrator for makers

Check: Are test, demo and abandoned agents unpublished or deleted? Does every agent have an owner, backup owner, purpose and review date?
Verify: Power Platform inventory; agent inventory; last-published date
Target: Review every 6 months. Red flag: orphaned live agents

Check: Is Application Insights connected, with sensitive conversation content excluded from logs? Does data policy control it?
Verify: Copilot Studio > Settings > Advanced; data policy connector Application Insights in Copilot Studio
Target: Approved telemetry only. Red flag: PII in logs

Check: For each agent list SharePoint sites, OneDrive, uploaded files, public websites, Dataverse tables, connectors, Graph connectors and Azure AI Search indexes.
Verify: Copilot Studio > Knowledge; Dataverse agent components; Power Platform inventory
Target: Every source has an owner and classification. Red flag: sources nobody owns

Check: Do the connected sites have broad access (Everyone except external users, large groups, anonymous links, broken inheritance)? Has a permissions review been done?
Verify: SharePoint admin center and access reviews; SharePoint Advanced Management; Purview data security posture reports (verify licensing)
Target: Permissions reflect business need. Red flag: HR or finance sites open to all staff

Check: Are Purview sensitivity labels applied to source content and respected by agents? Are DLP policies for Copilot and agents configured where available?
Verify: Purview labels, auto-labeling and DLP policy for Copilot (verify current capabilities)
Target: Sensitive content labeled and protected. Red flag: no labels on regulated data

Check: Does the agent require authentication so retrieval is trimmed to the signed-in user? Which sources are not trimmed per user (for example some uploaded files or maker-credential sources)?
Verify: Learn: Security FAQ and knowledge source docs; test with two users of different permission
Target: Per-user trimming proven by test. Red flag: everyone sees maker's view

Check: Is public-web knowledge limited to approved domains with endpoint filtering? Is Bing grounding intentionally on or off?
Verify: Data policy endpoint filtering; environment settings
Target: Allow-list only. Red flag: arbitrary web content as ground truth

Check: Which uploaded files contain sensitive content? Treat uploaded files as visible to anyone who can use the agent unless documented otherwise.
Verify: Agent Knowledge page; file inventory; test
Target: Sensitive files kept in controlled sources. Red flag: confidential documents uploaded to a widely shared agent

Check: Do Dataverse knowledge sources respect table and row security for the end user? Are Azure AI Search and Graph connector sources security-trimmed with user identity or a shared key?
Verify: Security roles; Azure AI Search configuration; test with low-privilege user
Target: User-context retrieval. Red flag: shared admin key

Check: Can the agent answer from general model knowledge, or only from knowledge sources? Are citations on? Is there a fallback and escalation path when no answer is found?
Verify: Agent generative answers settings and instructions
Target: Scope aligned to risk. Red flag: confident answers without sources in regulated processes

Check: Who owns content accuracy? How fast are changes reflected? Is stale content removed?
Verify: Content owners; sync schedule
Target: Named content owner. Red flag: outdated policy documents indexed

Check: List every tool per agent: connector actions, flows, custom connectors, MCP servers, HTTP nodes, child or connected agents.
Verify: Copilot Studio > Tools; solution components; Power Platform inventory
Target: Documented, minimal. Red flag: tools added speculatively

Check: Does each tool run with end-user credentials or maker credentials? Is the maker account high-privileged?
Verify: Tool settings; security scan; PPAC Control maker credential options
Target: End-user default. Red flag: maker admin account used by all users

Check: Which tools send email, update records, delete, approve or move money? Is there user confirmation or approval? Is there separation of read and write tools?
Verify: Tool list review; test conversation
Target: Confirmation for impactful actions. Red flag: agent can act on ambiguous user input

Check: Which agents run on triggers (email, SharePoint, schedule)? Under whose identity? What is the blast radius if triggered by malicious input? Are triggers controlled by the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector data policy?
Verify: Agent Triggers; data policy; credential settings. Note that enforcing end-user credentials will fail autonomous runs, so autonomy needs a deliberate identity design
Target: Autonomous use limited, monitored and approved. Red flag: triggers from external mailbox with broad permissions

Check: Which MCP servers are connected? Who hosts and owns them? How do they authenticate? Are tool descriptions and outputs trusted? Note blocking Power Platform connectors by data policy also blocks MCP tool access.
Verify: Agent tools; hosting inventory; data policy
Target: Approved servers with authentication. Red flag: public MCP server with write tools

Check: Are flows used as tools secured (no anonymous trigger, input validation, least privilege connections)?
Verify: Flow definition review
Target: Validated input. Red flag: flow trusts agent-provided parameters

Check: Are custom connectors reviewed (OpenAPI definition, auth, ownership, certification)? Are HTTP node endpoints allow-listed?
Verify: Custom connector inventory; endpoint filtering
Target: Reviewed catalog. Red flag: unauthenticated custom APIs

Check: Do child, connected or external agents have separate authorization boundaries and owners? Is identity passed securely?
Verify: Architecture review
Target: Clear permission boundaries. Red flag: privilege escalation through a trusted agent

Check: Are runaway loops, repeated tool calls and cost spikes limited?
Verify: Credit monitoring; test
Target: Limits and alerts. Red flag: unbounded autonomous runs

Check: What moderation level is configured per agent and per generative node? Is it reviewed for audience and use case? (Tenant-defined subject blocking is not provided, so use instructions and topic design.)
Verify: Agent generative AI settings; Learn security and governance note
Target: Documented setting per agent. Red flag: untested default

Check: Is the agent tested against direct user injection and indirect injection through documents, web pages, emails and tool output? Are tools unable to be manipulated into data leakage?
Verify: Red-team test script; sample attack library; review logs
Target: Pass criteria defined. Red flag: no adversarial tests

Check: Is there a test set with expected answers and automated evaluation? Is it run before each publish and after model or content changes?
Verify: Copilot Studio agent evaluation; test results history (automated evaluation using authenticated accounts uses the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector, so check data policy)
Target: Documented pass thresholds. Red flag: manual spot checks only

Check: Do instructions contain secrets, confidential policy text or contradictory rules? Are they version-controlled and peer-reviewed?
Verify: Agent instructions; Git history
Target: Reviewed prompts. Red flag: credentials in instructions

Check: For high-impact decisions or actions, is there approval, escalation to a human, and logging of the decision?
Verify: Process design; topic flow
Target: Human review for material actions. Red flag: automated decisions on individuals

Check: Has each agent been classified by impact (for example HR, legal, financial, health, safety)? Has a responsible AI review or DPIA been done where required?
Verify: Review records
Target: Higher risk means stronger controls. Red flag: no classification

Check: Do users know they are talking to AI, what sources are used and how to give feedback or escalate?
Verify: Greeting message, disclaimer, feedback buttons
Target: Disclosure present. Red flag: AI presented as a human

Check: Are unanswered, low-rated and escalated conversations reviewed? Is there a change process to fix gaps?
Verify: Analytics; feedback; transcripts
Target: Monthly quality review. Red flag: nobody reads analytics

Check: Is there a documented route to report, triage, pause and fix an unsafe agent response?
Verify: Incident runbook
Target: Defined owner and SLA. Red flag: no process

Check: Are production assets in solutions (managed in test and prod) with a defined publisher and versioning?
Verify: Solution inventory per environment; layers
Target: 100% of critical assets in managed solutions. Red flag: unmanaged customizations in prod

Check: Are deployments done through Power Platform pipelines, Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions with approvals, and a service principal rather than a person?
Verify: Pipeline configuration and run history
Target: Automated, auditable. Red flag: manual solution import by makers

Check: Are environment-specific values and connections externalized? Are secrets stored in Key Vault-backed variables?
Verify: Solution components; deployment settings file
Target: No hard-coded values. Red flag: edits after import

Check: Is solution source (unpacked) in Git? Is Copilot Studio Git integration or deploy-from-Git used where available?
Verify: Repository; Copilot Studio ALM guidance
Target: Reviewed pull requests. Red flag: no history

Check: Is solution checker run in pipelines and enforced in managed environments?
Verify: PPAC and pipeline settings
Target: Blocks on high severity. Red flag: optional

Check: Are there automated tests (Power Apps Test Engine, flow tests, agent evaluations) and user acceptance steps before release?
Verify: Test repositories and results
Target: Evidence for each release. Red flag: tested in production
